Theme

childhood noun

also boyhood, girlhood, in my childhood, from childhood, since childhood, early childhood, infancy

classical

Cic. Sen. 76: sunt pueritiae studia certa
Ter. Heaut. 183: jam inde ūsque ā pueritiā

pueritia, pueritiae f.

noun, first declension

childhood, boyhood

Childhood up to about the seventeenth year, though often used more loosely (Lewis & Short); after it comes adulēscentia (see youth). “From childhood” is ā pueritiā, or ā puerō, ā puerīs, “from a boy, from boys”. Horace scans it puertia (C. 1.36.8).

Other words

  • īnfantia, īnfantiae f. — infancy, early childhood

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 9.7: īnfantia dulcior; Quint. 1.1.19: quantum in īnfantiā praesūmptum est temporis

    First “inability to speak” (Lucr. 5.1031), and so infancy, early childhood (Lewis & Short).

  • ā parvulō — from early childhood, from a little boy

    phrase · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 48: ēdūxī ā parvulō

Examples

  • sunt pueritiae studia certa; num igitur ea dēsīderant adulēscentēs?

    childhood has its own pursuits; do young men miss them, then?Cic. Sen. 76

  • nam mihi magna cum eō jam inde ūsque ā pueritiā fuit semper familiāritās

    for he and I have always been close friends, right from childhoodTer. Heaut. 183–184

  • inde ego hunc majōrem adoptāvī mihi; ēdūxī ā parvulō

    so I adopted the elder one as my own; I brought him up from a little boyTer. Ad. 47–48

See also child, youth, since, early, life, little boy.
